coupling: The first edited commit derives column_nelems as the source element count divided by dims[0] (the product of the trailing dimensions) and uses it only for the rank-2 full-column test, where it is equivalent to dims[1]. That commit is therefore benign by itself. The later rank-N refactor promotes that derived value and overwrites dimp[rank - 2], the multiplier used for offsets in the last dimension. The correct last-dimension multiplier is the prefix product dims[0] * ... * dims[rank - 2], not the trailing product dims[1] * ... * dims[rank - 1]. For an in-contract 2 x 2 x 8 slab starting at last-dimension index 7, the composed code computes 7 * 16 instead of 7 * 4 and reads far beyond the 32-element source buffer. The unsafe value is introduced by one commit and consumed by the other, so a correct repair must reconcile the derived-count semantics with the rank-N prefix-product consumer rather than reviewing either diff in isolation.
